title: Letter from David Bailey, Charlotte Gerken and Rebecca Jackson on reaffirming the PRA's position and clarifying expectations on innovations in the use of deposits, e-money and stablecoins
summary: Letter to Chief Executive Officers of all banks and designated investment firms.
whyItMatters: Relevant for settlement assets, reserve models, payment stablecoin issuance, redemption rights and prudential or supervisory treatment.

title: Letter from David Bailey, Charlotte Gerken and Rebecca Jackson on the prudential treatment of tokenised assets, stablecoins, and other cryptoasset exposures
summary: Letter to Chief Executive Officers of all banks and designated investment firms.
whyItMatters: Relevant for settlement assets, reserve models, payment stablecoin issuance, redemption rights and prudential or supervisory treatment.

title: FCA sets landmark cryptoasset regime rules and confirms authorisation gateway timing
summary: The FCA announced landmark rules for the UK cryptoasset regime and confirmed that the authorisation gateway for firms is expected to open on 30 September 2026.
whyItMatters: Relevant for firms preparing to conduct regulated cryptoasset activities, including custody, trading platform activity, dealing, arranging, issuing and related market infrastructure services.

title: FCA publishes overview of cryptoasset regime policy statements
summary: The FCA published an overview page for policy statements applying to firms that carry out or intend to carry out regulated cryptoasset activities or designated activities under the Cryptoassets Regulations.
whyItMatters: This is a core implementation reference for UK firms assessing scope, authorisation preparation, conduct requirements and operational readiness.

title: FCA consults on cryptoasset perimeter guidance
summary: The FCA is consulting on proposed perimeter guidance for the UK future cryptoasset regime, intended to help firms understand when authorisation may be required.
whyItMatters: Perimeter guidance is likely to be one of the most important documents for deciding whether a product, service or platform activity falls within the future UK regime.

title: EBA consults on methodology for setting fines under MiCA
summary: The EBA consulted on draft methodology for setting fines under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation.
whyItMatters: Enforcement methodology affects issuers and service providers subject to MiCA oversight, especially significant ART and EMT issuers.

title: BIS Annual Economic Report discusses tokenisation and stablecoin limitations
summary: The BIS analysed tokenisation, programmable platforms and stablecoins, highlighting the role of trusted money and the limitations of current private stablecoin arrangements.
whyItMatters: Important for assessing whether tokenised settlement should rely on stablecoins, tokenised deposits, central bank money or new wholesale settlement architectures.

title: FSI summarises implementation of the FSB global regulatory framework for cryptoasset activities
summary: The FSI summarised global implementation progress for the FSB framework covering cryptoasset activities and global stablecoin arrangements.
whyItMatters: Useful for comparing implementation approaches across jurisdictions and identifying areas where regulatory divergence may affect cross-border market infrastructure.

title: Tokenisation as digital market infrastructure: from single-chain simplicity to 24/7 liquidity
summary: Finextra published a long-read discussing tokenisation as a form of digital market infrastructure and the operational frictions it may reduce.
whyItMatters: Useful market context for how tokenisation is being positioned around issuance, servicing, reconciliation, collateral and settlement workflows.

title: SEC Crypto Task Force tracks policy work on crypto asset markets
summary: The SEC Crypto Task Force page is a key public source for policy materials, written submissions and work on the application of federal securities laws to crypto asset markets.
whyItMatters: A key source for tracking U.S. policy development around registration pathways, disclosure, custody, market intermediaries and investor protection.

title: Basel Committee standard on prudential treatment of cryptoasset exposures
summary: The Basel Committee standard sets out the prudential treatment of banks' exposures to cryptoassets, including tokenised traditional assets, stablecoins and unbacked cryptoassets.
whyItMatters: Useful baseline for bank capital treatment, risk classification and internal policy discussions on direct or indirect cryptoasset exposures.

title: Ledger Insights provides institutional news on tokenisation, stablecoins and digital currency
summary: Ledger Insights is useful for enterprise blockchain, tokenised deposits, stablecoins, digital assets and capital markets infrastructure news.
whyItMatters: Good secondary source for identifying institutional pilots, market infrastructure projects and central-bank-adjacent developments.

title: GENIUS Act establishes U.S. federal framework for payment stablecoins
source: The White House / U.S. Federal Register
summary: The President signed S. 1582, the GENIUS Act, into law, creating a federal statutory framework for payment stablecoins in the United States.
whyItMatters: This is a core U.S. baseline for payment-stablecoin issuance, permitted issuers, reserve requirements, redemption expectations and state/federal supervisory pathways.

title: OCC proposes rules implementing the GENIUS Act for stablecoin issuance
source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency / Federal Register
summary: The OCC proposed a rule to implement the GENIUS Act for entities subject to OCC jurisdiction, including pathways for permitted payment stablecoin issuers.
whyItMatters: Relevant for banks, nonbank stablecoin issuers and service providers assessing U.S. stablecoin issuance, reserve custody, transition and supervisory requirements.

title: OCC Interpretive Letter 1183 reaffirms national bank authority for certain crypto-asset activities
source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
summary: OCC Interpretive Letter 1183 rescinded the prior supervisory nonobjection process and reaffirmed that crypto-asset custody, certain stablecoin and DLT activities discussed in earlier OCC letters remain permissible for national banks when conducted safely and lawfully.
whyItMatters: Important for U.S. bank engagement with crypto custody, stablecoin reserves and DLT payment activities, while keeping the focus on safe and sound risk management.

title: Federal Reserve withdraws prior crypto-asset and dollar-token guidance for banks
summary: The Federal Reserve withdrew prior guidance related to crypto-asset and dollar-token activities, including the advance-notification expectation for state member banks and the dollar-token supervisory nonobjection process.
whyItMatters: Significant for U.S. banks because crypto-asset activities are monitored through the normal supervisory process rather than the withdrawn notification/nonobjection guidance.

title: CFTC launches digital assets pilot program for tokenized collateral in derivatives markets
summary: The CFTC announced a digital assets pilot program and guidance on using certain tokenized assets, including BTC, ETH and USDC, as collateral in derivatives markets.
whyItMatters: Highly relevant for institutional collateral use cases, margin settlement, tokenized treasury collateral and regulated derivatives market infrastructure.

title: CFTC expands eligible tokenized collateral framework to payment stablecoins
summary: CFTC staff reissued and updated no-action relief to expand eligible tokenized collateral to include payment stablecoins issued by qualifying institutions.
whyItMatters: Strengthens the link between payment stablecoin regulation and collateral eligibility in regulated derivatives markets.

title: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin 121 addresses obligations to safeguard crypto-assets
summary: SAB 121 expressed SEC staff views on accounting and disclosure obligations for entities safeguarding crypto-assets for platform users.
whyItMatters: Historical baseline for understanding the 2022–2025 U.S. custody-accounting debate and the later significance of SAB 122.

title: U.S. banking agencies issue joint statement on crypto-asset risks to banking organizations
summary: Federal banking agencies issued a joint statement highlighting crypto-asset risks for banking organizations after the 2022 market turmoil.
whyItMatters: Useful historical marker for the earlier supervisory posture toward bank crypto-asset exposures and the subsequent 2025 withdrawal of the joint statements.

title: U.S. Treasury sets framework for international engagement on digital assets
summary: Treasury published a framework for international engagement on digital assets following the 2022 Executive Order on responsible development of digital assets.
whyItMatters: Provides a U.S. policy baseline for cross-border regulatory coordination, financial stability and international standard-setting engagement.

title: MiCA published in the Official Journal of the European Union
summary: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 on markets in crypto-assets was published in the Official Journal, establishing the EU-wide MiCA framework.
whyItMatters: Core EU baseline for issuers of crypto-assets, ARTs, EMTs and crypto-asset service providers.

title: MiCA stablecoin provisions begin applying to ARTs and EMTs
summary: MiCA provisions for asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens began applying before the full CASP regime.
whyItMatters: Key date for EU stablecoin issuance, reserve, authorisation and supervisory requirements.

title: MiCA becomes fully applicable across the European Union
summary: MiCA became fully applicable, including the framework for crypto-asset service providers and broader cryptoasset market conduct requirements.
whyItMatters: Primary EU go-live date for CASP authorisation, service provision, market abuse and disclosure obligations.

title: ESMA finalises guidance on when crypto-assets qualify as financial instruments
summary: ESMA released final materials on the conditions and criteria for qualifying crypto-assets as financial instruments under MiCA/MiFID II.
whyItMatters: Important for RWA and tokenised securities because the legal classification determines whether MiCA or existing securities law is the relevant regime.

title: FCA finalises UK financial promotion rules for qualifying cryptoassets
summary: The FCA published PS23/6 setting out financial promotion rules for cryptoassets marketed to UK consumers.
whyItMatters: Major UK milestone because cryptoasset promotions capable of having an effect in the UK were brought into a more formal conduct regime.

title: HM Treasury confirms final proposals for UK cryptoasset regulatory regime
summary: HM Treasury published its response and final proposals for bringing a number of cryptoasset activities into the UK financial services regulatory perimeter.
whyItMatters: The main UK policy bridge between earlier consultations and the detailed FCA regime now being implemented.

title: FSB finalises global regulatory framework for crypto-asset activities and stablecoins
summary: The FSB finalised recommendations forming a global framework for crypto-asset activities and global stablecoin arrangements.
whyItMatters: Important cross-jurisdictional baseline for supervisory consistency, global stablecoin oversight and financial stability expectations.

title: IOSCO finalises policy recommendations for crypto and digital asset markets
summary: IOSCO finalised policy recommendations for crypto and digital asset markets, covering intermediaries, custody, conflicts, market abuse and cross-border cooperation.
whyItMatters: Useful securities-regulator baseline for comparing local regimes against international expectations for market integrity and investor protection.

title: Basel Committee finalises disclosure framework and targeted amendments for cryptoasset exposures
summary: The Basel Committee published its final disclosure framework for banks cryptoasset exposures and targeted amendments to the cryptoasset standard.
whyItMatters: Important for banks because the disclosure framework and amendments are intended to be implemented from 1 January 2026.
